```{r include=FALSE,echo=FALSE}
source(file="fisherXY.R")
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
require(knitr)
require(foreign)
GSS <-read.dta(file="GSS2016.dta")
GSS <- droplevels(GSS)
mydata <- select(GSS,race,cappun)
mydata <- na.omit(mydata)
```

# Introduction

<!--In this section you explain what you are trying to show.  Where did the data come from?  What is the research or other question you are trying to answer?.  If you skimp in this section expect to be marked down in your grade. Paint a picture of the project a couple of paragraphs is expected!-->

Is attitude toward capitol punishment (cappun) independent of race (race)?
If not, then whose view differs from whom??

Data from GSS 2016. 

$H_0$ : Yes attitude towards capitol punishment is independent of race. In other words there's no difference... (-_-)

$H_A$ : No, attitude towards capitol punishment is NOT independent of race!!! AKA there is a difference in views!

## Descriptive Results

### Graphical Descriptive Results

```{r}
barchartGC(~race + cappun,data=mydata)
barchartGC(~race + cappun,data=mydata, type="percent")

```
These graphs suggest that white people have a higher percentage of being in favour of capital punishment, being the highest percentage out of the three race options, followed by "other" and lastly black people. This is from the second graph, assuming the first one factors in the population of said races.

## Now with The Most data (fewer variables gives more data points)



### Numerical Descriptive Results

<!--Numerical results go here. Use the numerical results to describe the patterns if any that exist in the data as focused toward the research question!-->

```{r}
table1 <- xtabs(~race + cappun, data=mydata)
rowPerc(table1)
colPerc(table1)
```
From these results we can see that white people do indeed have a higher percentage of favouring capital punishment when compared with the other races. Roughly 65% of white people favour capital punishment, whereas roughly 43% of black people favour it, and finally roughly 55% of people in the "other" race category favour it. Overall these results suggest that white people have the smallest percentage of being opposed to it.

## Now with More data


## Inferential Results

<!--State hypothesis clearly.  Make sure your discussion of the inferential test covers all the aspects that the test output produces, such as test statistic, p-value etc.  Make a decision about the null hypothesis, explain the assumptions on which the selected test/procedure was based, and why the chosen procedure satisfies the assumptions and is appropriate to answer the research question!-->

```{r}
fisherXY(mydata$race,mydata$cappun,confL=0.05) 
```
The fisherXY test shows that all races have a difference in favouring/not favouring capital punishment, as each one has a p value less than 0.05. So we can reject the null. They also each have different odds ratios.

## More data version


# Discussion and Conclusion

Original question: Is attitude toward capitol punishment (cappun) independent of race (race)?
If not, then whose view differs from whom??

Based on the fisherXY test which shows that each race has a differing relationship to favouring or not favouring capital punishment, we can reject the null that there is no difference between races and capital punishment. Each race has a difference relationship with these stats, with the following p values for the different races: 2.2e-16, 0.002607, and 0.001564. All of these are less than 0.05, which is why he can confidently reject the null and finish this crap up!!
